VERID_BURNT_AGENT_CONTEXT: Reviewer {target} requires fork_turns: none and only the module ACs, design path and diff.
VERID_BURNT_TOOL_UNSUPPORTED: Tool {target} is not in the supported tool list. verid cannot judge it.
VERID_BURNT_PATCH_UNSUPPORTED: Patch syntax is unsupported or malformed ({target}); no target may be written. Send patches with the apply_patch tool only, never through the shell.
VERID_BURNT_BASH_NESTED_CODEX: Starting a nested Codex session is not allowed ({target}).
cook.codex_trust: Codex: trust this project and every verid hook in /hooks before working; run verid doctor after changes.
VERID_BURNT_PLUGIN_PROTECTED: The agent may not change verid plugin sources, code or data ({target}). Only the developer manages plugins; /verid tip cannot allow this write.
VERID_BURNT_HALTED: The developer halted verid ({target}): every tool call is denied until they run `{verid} resume` in their own terminal. Stop now and tell the developer where the work stands.
VERID_BURNT_PLUGIN_IN_AGENT: Every verid plugin command belongs to the developer. Run it in your own terminal outside Claude Code.
VERID_BURNT_PLUGIN_CONFIRM: Plugin installation needs confirmation. Run in your own terminal or pass --yes after reviewing the source.
VERID_BURNT_PLUGIN_EVENT: Warning: plugin {name}, event {event}: {detail}. The verid decision is unchanged.
VERID_BURNT_PLUGIN_INTEGRITY: Plugin {name} failed its integrity check: {detail}. Its scripts will not run. Review the source and re-approve with verid plugin add (remove the installed copy first), or restore with verid cook / verid upgrade and confirmation.
usage.plugin: manage workflow plugins (add, remove, list, doctor, run)
plugin.unofficial: Unofficial plugin: its scripts run with your user permissions. Review the source before accepting.
VERID_BURNT_STATE_PROTECTED: Protected verid data ({target}): private state cannot be read or written. CLI-owned review packets may be read, never changed by agents.
VERID_BURNT_SECRET_PROTECTED: Reading or writing secret files is not allowed ({target}).
VERID_BURNT_TRANSCRIPT_PROTECTED: Accessing Claude Code transcripts is not allowed ({target}).
VERID_BURNT_HOOK_PROTECTED: The agent may not change Claude Code settings, MCP server lists (.claude.json, .mcp.json), agent definitions, skills, command definitions or plugins, or verid's installed code ({target}): they register and run hooks, commands and MCP servers, agent definitions determine roles, and skills or commands could claim an allowed namespace.
VERID_BURNT_MANIFEST_PROTECTED: The agent may not change the verid manifest ({target}). Only the developer edits this file.
VERID_BURNT_DOCS_PROTECTED: The agent may only read the developer's documents ({target}). Write findings to .verid/research.md or .verid/spec.md instead; only the developer adds or edits files in .verid/docs/.
VERID_BURNT_INSTRUCTIONS_PROTECTED: Keep the verid block in {target} unchanged. Use Write/Edit/MultiEdit to edit other content; only the developer opens an exception.
VERID_BURNT_SKILL_NOT_ALLOWED: Skill is outside the allowlist ({target}). The developer can extend allowed_skills in .verid/manifest.yaml or allow this exact call once.
VERID_BURNT_AGENT_NOT_ALLOWED: Agent dispatch is outside the allowlist ({target}). Use an agent mapped in roles or allowed_agents in .verid/manifest.yaml; only the developer opens an exception.
VERID_BURNT_BASH_NESTED_CLAUDE: Starting a nested Claude Code session is not allowed ({target}).
VERID_BURNT_BASH_DEVELOPER_ONLY: The agent may not run verid's developer commands or its hook, or change CLAUDECODE ({target}): `cook`, `upgrade`, `garnish`, `stock`, `order`, `serve` and `plugin` are the developer's, run from their own terminal, and only Claude Code runs the hook. Ask the developer to run the command.
VERID_BURNT_BASH_DANGEROUS: The agent may not download or decode code and run it in one command, skip or redirect Git hooks, or raise privileges ({target}). Download to a file the developer can read, run project scripts as they are, commit through the hooks, and leave sudo, RunAs and setuid to the developer.
VERID_BURNT_SHELL_UNSUPPORTED: verid cannot read commands run through {target}, so it blocks them. Use the Bash tool, which verid judges.
VERID_BURNT_PAYLOAD: Invalid hook payload ({detail}). verid blocks to stay safe.
VERID_BURNT_INTERNAL: verid internal error ({detail}). verid blocks to stay safe.
VERID_BURNT_STATE_MISSING: verid state not found at {path}. The developer sets verid up by running `{verid} cook` in this project, from their own terminal. Until then every tool call is blocked.
VERID_BURNT_STATE_CORRUPT: verid state is corrupt ({path}). The developer must inspect and fix this file outside the agent.
VERID_BURNT_STATE_VERSION: verid state is from an unsupported verid version ({path}). verid does not guess or upgrade its shape; outside the agent, the developer deletes it and runs `verid cook` for a fresh state.
VERID_BURNT_LOCK_TIMEOUT: Could not acquire the state lock within {ms} ms ({path}). verid blocks to stay safe; try again.
VERID_BURNT_OVERRIDE_UNATTENDED: Only a developer typing in an interactive session can create an override. Prompts from subagents or `claude -p` sessions are rejected.
VERID_BURNT_OVERRIDE_USAGE: Usage: `/verid tip <reason>` to request an exception for the action that was just blocked, then `/verid confirm <code>` to accept the risk.
VERID_BURNT_OVERRIDE_NOTHING: Nothing was just blocked, or no warning is pending, in this session to override.
VERID_BURNT_OVERRIDE_FORBIDDEN: {rule} is an invariant and cannot be overridden ({target}). The developer must do this outside the agent.
VERID_BURNT_OVERRIDE_BAD_CODE: Wrong confirmation code. No override was created.
VERID_BURNT_OVERRIDE_STALE: The blocked action changed since the warning. The old warning was cancelled; type `/verid tip <reason>` again.
VERID_BURNT_TDD_NO_FAILING_TEST: Production code is locked while the TDD cycle is RAW ({target}). No production code without a failing test first: write or fix a test, run `{verid} taste`, and check that it fails for the reason you expect. If this conversation only refactors, with every test passing, the developer can run `{verid} garnish` from their own terminal.
VERID_BURNT_TDD_TEST_FROZEN: Tests are frozen while the TDD cycle is COOKING ({target}): a test is failing, and only production code may make it pass. Write the minimum production code, then run `{verid} taste`. If the failing test itself is wrong, stop and tell the developer why.
VERID_BURNT_PLAN_NOT_APPROVED: Production code is locked until the developer approves a module of the plan ({target}). Write or finish the module in .verid/plan.md: a `## Module: <name>` heading, then one `- AC-1: …` line per acceptance criterion, and `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]` where something is unclear (ask the developer about it). Then ask the developer to run `{verid} order <module>` from their own terminal. Changing the open module's section after approval locks production code again, and so does serving the last open module.
VERID_BURNT_PLAN_NO_RESEARCH: Audit: plan written before research ({target}). Follow .verid/rules/workflow.md; this warning does not block writing.
VERID_BURNT_PLAN_NO_SPEC: Audit: plan written before the spec ({target}). Follow .verid/rules/workflow.md; this warning does not block writing.
VERID_BURNT_PLAN_NO_DESIGN: Audit: plan written before design ({target}). Follow .verid/rules/workflow.md; this warning does not block writing.
VERID_BURNT_ROLE_READ_ONLY: {target}: the reviewer ({writer}) writes nothing; verid records its final report when it stops.
VERID_BURNT_ROLE_DOC_ONLY: {target}: {writer} may write only {document}. Return questions and options to the main conversation; it asks the developer.
VERID_BURNT_ROLE_QA_E2E_ONLY: {target}: qa ({qa}) writes only end-to-end tests: paths matching e2e_globs. This call came from {writer}. The TDD gate still applies.
VERID_BURNT_ROLE_TESTER_ONLY: {target} is a test: only tester ({tester}) writes it; this call came from {writer}.
VERID_BURNT_ROLE_CODER_ONLY: {target} is production code: only coder ({coder}) writes it; this call came from {writer}.
VERID_BURNT_AUTO_STUCK: Production code and tests are locked because the auto drive is stuck ({target}). `{verid} menu` says why. Do not look for a way around it: only the developer can clear it, by running `{verid} order` from their own terminal.
VERID_BURNT_AUTO_NO_MODULE: Production code is locked while no module is open ({target}). The auto drive opens modules itself once the design is signed and the plan passes review: ask the developer to sign the design with `{verid} order` from their own terminal, write `.verid/plan.md` ending with the `product` module, then have the reviewer check the plan.
VERID_BURNT_AUTO_WAITING_MERGE: Production code, tests, and the history and pushes of the closed module's branch are locked while it waits for the developer's squash-merge ({target}). Nothing is left for the agent: stop here. The developer pushes the branch, squash-merges its pull request and updates the local main; at the agent's next stop or the next session's start verid finds the squash and opens the next module itself. Lifting this once does not merge, serve or open anything, and the role, TDD and no-open-module rules still judge the write.
VERID_BURNT_AUTO_BRANCH: Production code and tests are locked until verid has made the next auto module's branch ({target}). It makes it at the agent's next stop or the next session's start; when Git does not allow it (a branch of that name already exists, main has no commit, the project is outside Git, or Git cannot carry the changes in the working tree), Stop says what the developer has to settle. Do not look for a way around it: verid never discards work to make the branch.
VERID_BURNT_GIT_MAIN_COMMIT: Main's history is the developer's: commits, merges, rebases, resets and other changes to main are not allowed ({target}). Work on a branch from main named feat/, fix/, chore/, docs/, refactor/ or test/ plus a name, for example `git switch -c feat/<module>`; the developer integrates it through a pull request and updates main.
VERID_BURNT_GIT_BRANCH_NAME: Work branches start with feat/, fix/, chore/, docs/, refactor/ or test/, then a name ({target}). Create or rename the branch that way, from main, for example `git switch -c fix/<slug>`.
VERID_BURNT_GIT_PROTECTED_PUSH: Pushing to a protected ref is not allowed ({target}): main and the manifest's `git.protected_refs` change only through pull requests. Push the work branch itself, for example `git push -u origin HEAD:refs/heads/feat/<module>`, and leave the pull request and merge to the developer.
VERID_BURNT_GIT_INTERNALS: Writing inside a repository's .git folder is not allowed ({target}): its refs, configuration and hooks decide what main is and what Git runs. Use Git commands, which verid judges; a change there is the developer's.
VERID_BURNT_GIT_UNRESOLVED: verid cannot tell which repository, branch or ref this Git command reaches, so it blocks it ({target}). Run that Git command on its own with literal paths and refs (for example `git -C api commit`, without variables, aliases, -c or extra repository options). If main itself cannot be told, ask the developer to set `default_branch` in `.verid/manifest.yaml` or to create main.
VERID_BURNT_MANIFEST_MISSING: verid manifest not found at {path}. `{verid} taste` needs it: the developer creates it with `{verid} cook --mode <prep|recipe|remix>` from their own terminal, adding --test-cmd, --src and --tests when verid does not recognise the project.
VERID_BURNT_MANIFEST_INVALID: verid manifest is invalid ({path}): {detail}. Only the developer can fix this file; until then every file write is blocked.
VERID_BURNT_RUN_EXIT_MISMATCH: The test command exited with {exit} while the JUnit report has {failed} failing test(s). verid does not trust a run whose exit code and report disagree. This run is not evidence; the TDD state is unchanged.
VERID_BURNT_RUN_NO_JUNIT: The test command left no readable JUnit report at {path}. If the output shows a runner or library missing (no `npm install` yet, pytest not installed…), install it and run again; a test_cmd the developer set must write the report to {junit}. This run is not evidence; the TDD state is unchanged.
VERID_BURNT_RUN_NO_TESTS: The JUnit report at {path} has no test that ran: write a test, or see in the output why the runner found none. This run is not evidence; the TDD state is unchanged.
VERID_BURNT_RUN_TIMEOUT: The test command was still running after {seconds} s, so verid stopped it. This run is not evidence; the TDD state is unchanged. A test command in watch mode never ends; if the suite really needs longer, the developer raises timeout_sec in the manifest.
VERID_BURNT_RUN_STALE: Production code or a test was written, or the TDD state changed, while this run was in progress, so the run may not include the latest changes. This run is not evidence; the TDD state is unchanged. Run `{verid} taste` again.
VERID_BURNT_RUN_NO_BASELINE: No baseline is recorded for this remix project, so `{verid} taste` ran nothing and the TDD state is unchanged. The developer records the tests that already fail by running `{verid} stock` from their own terminal; until then production code stays locked.
VERID_BURNT_RUN_NO_RUNNER: The project has no test runner verid can run by itself yet, so nothing ran; the TDD state is unchanged and production code stays locked. Set the project and its test runner up first: a package.json with vitest or jest, a pyproject.toml with pytest, a pom.xml, a build.gradle, a .csproj or .sln, a go.mod, a composer.json with phpunit, or a Gemfile with rspec. The next `{verid} taste` finds it.{detail}
VERID_BURNT_RUN_RUNNER_GONE: verid ran {runners} before and does not find it now: its build file is gone, or no longer names it. Nothing ran: without that runner its tests, failing ones included, would leave every run. Put the build file or the runner back. If the developer really drops that runner, they run `{verid} cook` again in their own terminal.
VERID_BURNT_INIT_INVALID: verid cook cannot use {path} ({detail}) and changed nothing: fix it, then run verid cook again.
VERID_BURNT_INSTRUCTIONS_LINKED: verid cannot write {path}: the instruction file must not be a symbolic link. Use a regular file, then run verid cook or upgrade again.
VERID_BURNT_INIT_UNSTABLE: Setup changed during all three checks. Nothing was written. Pause edits to the setup files, then retry `{verid} cook` or `{verid} upgrade`.
VERID_BURNT_INIT_NO_MODE: verid cook needs --mode for a new manifest: prep (a new project), recipe (a spec says what to build) or remix (code exists). This folder looks like {suggested}: run `{verid} cook --mode {suggested}` to confirm. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_INIT_IN_AGENT: verid cook and upgrade run only from the developer's own terminal, not inside Claude Code (CLAUDECODE is set): the agent must not be able to set verid up again. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_REFACTOR_IN_AGENT: verid garnish runs only from the developer's own terminal, not inside Claude Code: only the developer declares that a conversation only refactors. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_HALT_IN_AGENT: Only the developer halts or resumes verid, from their own terminal: not from Claude Code or Codex.
VERID_BURNT_REFACTOR_NOT_GREEN: Refactoring needs every test passing, and the last `{verid} taste` did not pass (or there is none yet). Run `{verid} taste` until it passes, then try again. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_BASELINE_IN_AGENT: verid stock runs only from the developer's own terminal, not inside Claude Code: only the developer decides which failures were there before verid. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_MODE_MISMATCH: `{verid} {command}` is not available in mode {mode}: `stock` is for remix, `order` and `serve` are for prep and recipe. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_APPROVE_IN_AGENT: verid order runs only from the developer's own terminal, not inside Claude Code: only the developer approves the acceptance criteria the tests have to cover. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_PLAN_MISSING: There is no plan at {path}, so there is nothing to approve. The agent writes the modules there, each a `## Module: <name>` heading with its acceptance criteria, one per line as `- AC-1: <what it does>`, and asks the developer about anything unclear; then the developer runs `{verid} order` again. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_DESIGN_MISSING: There is no design at {path}, so there is nothing for the order to sign. The agent writes how the project is built there (architecture, data, interfaces), agreed with the developer (verid:design); then the developer runs `{verid} order` again.
VERID_BURNT_RESEARCH_MISSING: There is no research at {path}, so there is nothing for the order to sign. The agent asks the developer what the project is for, who uses it and how it should work, one question at a time, and writes the answers there; then the developer runs `{verid} order` again.
VERID_BURNT_PLAN_INVALID: verid order cannot approve {path} ({detail}) and changed nothing. A plan lists modules, each a `## Module: <name>` heading followed by its acceptance criteria, one per line as `- AC-1: <what it does>`, with no code repeated and no [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] left in the module. Fix the plan, then run `{verid} order` again.
VERID_BURNT_MODULE_REQUIRED: This plan has several modules ({modules}): say which one to approve, as `{verid} order <module>`. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_MODULE_UNKNOWN: There is no module {module} in .verid/plan.md (modules: {modules}). Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_MODULE_OPEN: Module {module} is still open, and only one module is worked on at a time. Finish it and have the developer serve it with `{verid} serve {module}`, or edit or remove its section in .verid/plan.md to set it aside. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_SERVE_IN_AGENT: Only the developer serves a module, from their own terminal: `{verid} serve` refuses to run inside Claude Code. Ask the developer to run it.
VERID_BURNT_SERVE_NOT_READY: Module {module} cannot be served yet: {detail}. A module is served once it is approved and open, every one of its acceptance criteria has a passing test, and the last `{verid} taste` passed with no change after it. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_PRODUCT_TOO_EARLY: The product module comes last: it says the whole product works end to end, so every other module is served first. Not served yet: {modules}.
VERID_BURNT_AUTO_ORDER_MODULE: The auto drive opens the modules itself, in the order of the plan, so `{verid} order` takes no module name. `{verid} order` alone signs the research and the design, or continues a drive that is stuck. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_AUTO_SERVE: The auto drive serves a module itself once its tests pass, the reviewer has passed it and the project is committed, so there is nothing for `{verid} serve` to do. `{verid} menu` says what is still missing. Nothing was changed.
VERID_BURNT_ARCHITECTURE_FAILED: Audit: architecture check of repo {repo} failed. Log: {log}. Assess it against .verid/rules/architecture.md and run `{verid} taste` after any fix. This warning does not block module closure.
VERID_BURNT_ARCHITECTURE_STALE: Audit: no architecture result for repo {repo}. Run `{verid} taste` to observe its checker after passing tests. This warning does not block module closure.
VERID_BURNT_ARCHITECTURE_UNAVAILABLE: Audit: architecture check of repo {repo} is unavailable: {detail}. Restore the command, then run `{verid} taste`. This warning does not block module closure.
VERID_BURNT_GIT_WORK_BASE: Module {module} cannot close: the start of its work in repo {repo} cannot be trusted ({detail}), so its commits cannot be checked. A module ordered before verid recorded where work starts needs the developer to run `{verid} order {module}` again; work that no longer descends from the recorded main commit has to be rebased onto it, or the developer decides how to recover.
VERID_BURNT_GIT_COMMIT_MESSAGE: Module {module} cannot close: commit {commit} in repo {repo} is not a Conventional Commit (`<type>[(scope)][!]: <description>`, then a blank line before any body): "{header}". Reword it on the work branch (`git commit --amend` for the last commit), then have the module reviewed again.
hint.overridable: Follow the refusal; an exception needs the developer's `/verid tip <reason>`.
override.risk_warning: RISK WARNING. You are about to let the agent bypass rule {rule} exactly once for: {tool} {target}. Reason: {reason}. The override works once, for this exact action only, and is recorded in the audit log. To accept the risk, type: /verid confirm {code}
override.created: verid: the developer allowed {tool} {target} exactly once. Retry exactly that action, unchanged. Every other action is still blocked.
prompt.hook_failed: verid failed while handling the prompt ({detail}). The prompt was still sent; no override was created.
session.drafter: Dispatch the mapped {role} to draft {document}: it proposes before writing and returns questions with 2–3 options, trade-offs and a recommendation. The main conversation presents the proposal and relays each question to the developer.
session.qa: Dispatch the mapped qa for (e2e) ACs: it writes failing tests only in e2e_globs, reads selectors from real UI source and hands failures or stubs to the coder. The TDD gate still applies.
drive.auto: Drive auto: after the developer signs research/design, follow `{verid} menu` through verid:plan, verid:build and verid:review. Put blockers in .verid/blocked.md; three failed rounds or idle stops leave the drive stuck.
status.raw: RAW: production code is locked. Write one failing test for the next behaviour, check with the test runner that it fails on an assertion, for the reason you expect (a test that cannot load opens a stub step, `RAW · stub`), then run `{verid} taste`: once recorded, a failing test is frozen until it passes.
status.cooking: COOKING: write the minimum production code to make the failing tests pass, then run `{verid} taste`. Fix the code, not the test: tests are frozen until they pass. If a failing test is wrong, tell the developer.
status.plated: PLATED: all tests pass. Clean up the production code without adding behaviour, and keep `{verid} taste` passing. New behaviour starts with a failing test: writing the next test starts a new cycle in RAW.
status.stub: RAW · stub: a new test fails without reaching an assertion (it cannot load, or it crashes), so it is not RED yet. Production code is open only for the stub that lets it run: an empty function, a class, a wrong return value, no real behaviour. Then run `{verid} taste`: it must fail on an assertion. A stub that makes the test pass sends the cycle back to RAW.
status.off: The TDD gate is off: there is no .verid/manifest.yaml, so the hook applies only the file-protection rules. The developer creates the manifest to turn the gate on.
status.no_hooks: verid's hooks are not registered on this machine, so nothing is enforced here: the developer runs `{verid} cook` in this project, from their own terminal.
status.no_baseline: No baseline yet: the developer runs `{verid} stock` from their own terminal to record the tests that already fail. Until then `{verid} taste` refuses to run. A project with no test yet needs one first: write a test that passes and pins down what the code does today.
status.menu: The plan, its modules and the next step: `{verid} menu`.
status.last_refused: The last `{verid} taste` ({run}) did not count as evidence [{code}]:
stop.green: The last `{verid} taste` failed; the work is unfinished. Continue with verid:build or report the blocker. This hold is once per conversation.
stop.unverified: Code or tests changed after the last `{verid} taste`; the latest change has no run. Continue with verid:tdd or report the blocker. This hold is once per conversation.
stop.stub: The last `{verid} taste` failed because a test could not load or crashed, so the work is not done: finish the stub so that the test fails on an assertion, then run `{verid} taste`. If you are blocked, tell the developer what blocks you; verid lets you stop the next time.
stop.uncovered: Approved acceptance criteria still have no passing test: {acs}. Write a test for each, with the AC code in its name, and run `{verid} taste` until it passes. If you are blocked, tell the developer what blocks you. verid holds this once per conversation, so the next time you stop it goes through.
stop.evaluate: Every AC of module {module} passes. Review with {reviewer} via verid:review before the developer runs `{verid} serve {module}`. — means the reviewer role needs mapping. This hold is once per conversation.
tdd.passed_in_red: No test failed, so this run is not RAW (RED) evidence. Write a new test, or extend the one you just changed, so that it fails for the behaviour you want next.
tdd.stub_passed: The test passed once the stub was in, so it never failed on an assertion and proves nothing yet. Strengthen it until it fails for the behaviour you want, then run `{verid} taste`.
tdd.one_behaviour: {count} new tests fail at once. TDD takes one behaviour at a time: make one pass before writing the next, or tell the developer why these belong together.
tdd.no_new_failure: Tests failed, but only in ways the last run already showed, so nothing proves that the test you wrote or changed fails. Make it fail for the behaviour you want, then run `{verid} taste`.
tdd.baseline_known: {count} test(s) were already failing before verid (baseline). They are known failures and stay out of the TDD cycle: this run is judged without them, and they are not yours to fix.
tdd.baseline_changed: Warning: baseline test {test} still fails, but now with another first line: {line}. It may fail for a different reason than before; tell the developer.
tdd.baseline_left: {count} baseline test(s) pass now and left the baseline. If one fails again, it counts as a new failure.
usage.cook: set verid up for this project and machine
usage.upgrade: refresh setup and add missing manifest defaults
usage.doctor: check repos, runners, hooks and plugins without writes
usage.taste: run the tests, record the result as evidence
usage.menu: the plan, its modules and the next step
usage.order: approve a module of the plan
usage.serve: close the module once every AC passes
usage.stock: record the failing tests as the baseline
usage.garnish: open a conversation that only refactors
usage.halt: deny every agent tool call until resume (kill switch)
halt.done: Every agent tool call is now denied, and no Stop is held. Run `{verid} resume` to go on.
resume.done: Agents' tool calls are judged by every verid rule again.
halt.notice: The developer halted verid: every tool call is denied. Do not retry or work around it; tell the developer where the work stands and wait for `{verid} resume`.
usage.in_claude: In Claude Code, type /verid:  tip · confirm · peek · menu
usage.unknown: verid has no command {command}. The commands:
usage.unexpected: verid {command} does not take {args}. How to run it:
usage.no_module: verid serve needs the module to close: {verid} serve <module>.
init.done:
✅ verid is set up for this project and this machine.
   📌 Commit:         .verid/manifest.yaml  .verid/.gitignore  .claude/commands/verid/  {instructions}
   🚫 Do not commit:  .claude/settings.local.json (it names this machine's verid)
   👥 Teammates: after cloning, install verid and run `{verid} cook` once.
init.flags_ignored: The manifest already exists, so --mode, --drive, --layout, --provider, --iterations, --duration, --start-date, --demo-day, --test-cmd, --src and --tests were ignored: the developer edits .verid/manifest.yaml by hand.
init.shared_hooks: .claude/settings.json registers verid hooks too (set up by hand), so they would run twice. Remove verid's entries from .claude/settings.json; verid cook keeps its own in .claude/settings.local.json.
init.runners_forgotten: verid forgets the runners it no longer finds: {runners}. Their tests no longer run.
init.upgrade: This manifest was written by an older verid. Run `{verid} cook` in your own terminal to make the changes below (verid asks before writing): + adds this verid's defaults. Lines you added stay, test_cmd included. Adding roles splits the work: the main conversation then dispatches the tester and the coder instead of writing tests and code itself.
baseline.done: Baseline recorded: {count} test(s) were already failing before verid. They count as known failures, not as the agent's to fix. A baseline test that passes later leaves the baseline, and `{verid} taste` never adds to it.
baseline.no_tests: verid stock records the tests that already fail, and no test ran here. Have the agent write a first test that passes and pins down what the code does today (a characterization test), then run `{verid} stock` again.
approve.done: Module {module} approved: {acs}. The approval is for its section of .verid/plan.md as it is now: if that section changes, the developer approves it again with `{verid} order {module}`. Put the AC code in the name of each test that covers it, for example `AC-1 adds two numbers`, or `AC_1_addsTwoNumbers` where a name cannot hold a dash.
serve.done: Module {module} is served: every one of its acceptance criteria has a passing test, and the developer accepted it. Production code is locked again until the next module is approved.
menu.research: Next: clarify scope and constraints with verid:ba; record .verid/research.md.
menu.spec: Next: write what the project must do as traceable requirements with verid:ba; record .verid/spec.md.
menu.design: Next: agree architecture, data and interfaces with verid:design; record .verid/design.md.
menu.ask: Next: use verid:ba in the main conversation to ask the open questions above, one at a time, with 2–4 options, tradeoffs and your recommendation. Record Q → A in `.verid/research.md` under Clarifications and replace each plan marker with the answer and why. A changed module waits for `{verid} order <module>` again.
menu.split: Next: split the work into modules in `.verid/plan.md`, each a `## Module: <name>` heading with its acceptance criteria, one per line as `- AC-1: <what it does>` (verid:design, verid:plan). Ask the developer about anything unclear.
menu.cook: Next: build module {module} with verid:build; tester {tester}, coder {coder}. — means main handles an unmapped role.
menu.evaluate: Next: evaluate module {module} with verid:review; reviewer {reviewer}, then security {security} when mapped. Required reviews precede `{verid} serve {module}`. A reviewer shown as — needs roles.reviewer mapped.
menu.order: Next: ask the developer to read module {module} in `.verid/plan.md` and approve it with `{verid} order {module}` from their own terminal.
menu.served: Next: every module is served. For more work, add a module to `.verid/plan.md` and ask the developer to approve it.
menu.done: Next: the product module is served, so the product is done. For more work, add a module to `.verid/plan.md` and ask the developer to approve it.
menu.invalid: Next: fix .verid/plan.md ({detail}). Until it reads, no module is open and production code stays locked.
menu.remix: remix has no plan or modules: tests that already failed sit in the baseline (`{verid} stock`), and new work follows the TDD cycle. See `{verid} peek`.
auto.sign: Next: the research and the design are written, but the developer has not signed them, so the auto drive has not started. Ask the developer to read `.verid/research.md` and `.verid/design.md` and sign them with `{verid} order` from their own terminal. Until they do, production code stays locked.
auto.signed: Research and design signed. Agents review the plan, then build, review and serve modules in order. A stuck drive locks production code and tests; settle what `{verid} menu` names and run `{verid} order` to resume. Research/design changes produce audit warnings without stopping the drive.
auto.plan: Next: write `.verid/plan.md` from the signed design (verid:plan): one `## Module: <name>` heading per module, in the order they are built, each with its acceptance criteria one per line as `- AC-1: <what it does>`, and the `product` module last with every AC marked `(e2e)`. Answer each `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` yourself and write down why, unless the answer changes the design or only the developer knows it: then write what you need into `.verid/blocked.md` and stop.
auto.plan_fix: Next: fix `.verid/plan.md` ({detail}), then have the reviewer check it again. Until the plan passes review, no module is open and production code stays locked.
auto.plan_review: Next: have reviewer ({reviewer}) check .verid/plan.md against .verid/design.md via verid:review. A reviewer shown as — needs roles.reviewer mapped; the plan stays locked until review passes.
auto.review: Next: review module {module} with reviewer ({reviewer}) via verid:review. Required passing reviews of the latest work let verid serve it; commits are advisory.
auto.commit: Next: module {module} has uncommitted changes. Commit every change in the project, new files included, on the module's work branch with a Conventional Commit message, before the review: a review covers the committed work, and a commit after it needs another review. verid serves the module itself once the review of the committed work passes.
auto.fix: Next: the reviewer failed module {module}. Address its findings via verid:build (tester {tester}, coder {coder}), then reviewer {reviewer}. Three failed reviews leave the drive stuck.
auto.security: Next: have the security reviewer ({security}) check module {module} (verid:security): it reads the module's diff for vulnerabilities and exposed secrets, and changes nothing. Its final report must end with a line `Verdict: pass` or `Verdict: fail`. When it passes and the tree is committed, verid serves the module itself.
auto.security_fix: Next: security failed module {module}. Address its findings via verid:build (tester {tester}, coder {coder}), then reviewer {reviewer} and security {security}. Three failed security reviews leave the drive stuck.
auto.closed: verid served module {module} itself: every one of its acceptance criteria has a passing test, the reviewer passed it and its work is committed.
auto.preparing: Next: verid makes module {module}'s branch from the local main at the agent's next stop; if it cannot, it says what the developer has to settle in Git first.
auto.waiting_merge: Module {module} is closed on its own branch and waits for the developer: push each changed branch (repos: {repos}), open one pull request per branch, squash-merge it and update the local main. verid finds the squash commit on the local main by itself and then opens the next module from that main. Nothing is left for the agent: stop here.
auto.branch_problem: verid cannot prepare branch {branch} for module {module} in {repo}: {detail}. The developer settles this in Git; verid tries again at the agent's next stop or the next session's start, and never discards work to do it.
auto.integration_unclear: verid cannot yet tell whether module {module} was integrated in {repo}: {detail}. It keeps waiting; if the squash had to differ from the closed branch, the developer acknowledges the integration with `{verid} order` while the drive is not stuck.
auto.integrated: verid found module {module}'s squash commit on the local main ({commits}) and opens the next module from there.
auto.released: Module {module} changed no file in any repository, so there is nothing to merge: verid released its wait.
auto.acknowledged: The developer's order released module {module}'s wait for its merge: the drive goes on from the local main.
auto.done: Next: the product module was served and merged last, so the auto drive is done and you may stop. For more work, agree it with the developer first: a new module goes into `.verid/plan.md` before `product`, and the plan is reviewed again; a change to the research or the design stops the drive until the developer signs it with `{verid} order`.
auto.stuck.blocked: The auto drive is stuck: it was reported blocked ({detail}). The developer reads that, settles what it asks for, then runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
auto.stuck.research_changed: The auto drive is stuck: {detail} is no longer the research the developer signed. The developer reads what changed and, if they accept it, runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
auto.stuck.design_changed: The auto drive is stuck: {detail} is no longer the design the developer signed. The developer reads what changed and, if they accept it, runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue; the plan is then reviewed against the new design.
auto.stuck.served_changed: The auto drive is stuck: module {detail} was served, and its section of `.verid/plan.md` was edited or removed afterwards. Continuing reopens that module to be built and reviewed again, or forgets it if the plan no longer has it. The developer reads the edit, then runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
auto.stuck.plan_reviews: The auto drive is stuck: the reviewer has failed the plan {detail} times. The developer reads the reviewer's report and `.verid/plan.md`, settles what keeps failing (often the design itself), then runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
auto.stuck.coder_rounds: The auto drive is stuck: the coder has used up its rounds on {detail}, and a test that names it still fails. The developer reads that test and the code, decides whether the AC, the test or the design is wrong, then runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
auto.stuck.module_reviews: The auto drive is stuck: the reviewer has failed the open module {detail} times. The developer reads the reviewer's report, settles what keeps failing, then runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
auto.stuck.security_reviews: The auto drive is stuck: the security reviewer has failed the open module {detail} times. The developer reads the security reviewer's report, settles what keeps failing, then runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
auto.stuck.no_progress: The auto drive is stuck: Stop held the agent {detail} times in a row and nothing progressed: the tests, the plan, the commits and the counters did not change. The developer looks at what the agent is waiting for, then runs `{verid} order` from their own terminal to continue.
init.codex_done: Codex instructions saved. Commit .verid/manifest.yaml, .verid/.gitignore and {instructions}. Teammates run `{verid} cook` after cloning.
workspace.codex_done: Codex workspace instructions saved. Commit shared files inside .verid/ with `git -C .verid`; keep {instructions} at the workspace root as per-machine files. cook regenerates their verid blocks. Teammates run `{verid} cook` after cloning.
cook.codex_served: Codex hooks and AGENTS.md are ready. Trust this project and every verid hook in /hooks, then run verid doctor.
cook.mode.prep: a new dish from scratch — a new project, only an idea
cook.mode.recipe: cooking from a recipe — a specification already exists
cook.mode.remix: reworking a known dish — code and tests already exist
cook.drive.human: you do — you approve each module before it is cooked
cook.iterations_fixed: Each iteration lasts 14 days; demo is on its last day.
cook.upgrade: The manifest was written by an older verid. Make the changes above? (+ adds this verid's defaults; your test_cmd stays) Adding roles splits the work: the main conversation then dispatches the tester and the coder instead of writing tests and code itself.
cook.upgrade_no: Keep the manifest as it is
cook.runner_later: Let verid find it later, once the project has a build file
cook.runners: Test runner: verid finds it at each `taste`; it sees {runners} now.
cook.e2e_split: Both vitest or jest and Playwright run here, and by default each picks up the other's files: set `testDir: "e2e"` in playwright.config and exclude `e2e/**` in the vitest or jest config. `verid taste` runs both every time; set `test_cmd` for a faster loop.
cook.roles: Roles: the manifest maps verid's own agents (verid:tester, verid:coder, verid:reviewer), so the main conversation dispatches them to write tests and code, and `{verid} serve` asks for the reviewer's report. Install them once on this machine: `claude plugin marketplace add anhtranhai835/verid`, then `claude plugin install verid@verid`. Any other agent can fill a role: map it in `roles`.
cook.mapped_roles: Roles: dispatch the agents mapped in roles ({agents}); `{verid} serve` needs the reviewer's report. Install verid's agents once on this machine: `claude plugin marketplace add anhtranhai835/verid`, then `claude plugin install verid@verid`. Any other agent can fill a role: map it in `roles`.
cook.no_runner: Test runner: none yet. verid finds it at the first `taste` once the project has a build file (package.json, pyproject.toml, pom.xml, build.gradle, .csproj, go.mod…).
cook.pick_number: There is no {part} in the list (1–{count}). Type again, or press Enter to keep them as they are.
cook.pick_glob: {part} will not work: {detail}. Type again, or press Enter to keep them as they are.
cook.own_command: Type my own command… (it must contain {junit}, where the JUnit report goes)
cook.lock_code: Locked until a test fails: every code file that is not a test, in any folder
cook.lock_tests: Counted as tests: test/, tests/, spec/ and __tests__/ folders, and *.test.*, *.spec.*, *_test.*, test_*.* files
cook.lock_free: Not locked: documents, data and config (.md, .json, .yaml, *.config.*, dotfiles…), build and dependency files (.csproj, go.mod, build.gradle, Dockerfile, Makefile…), images, build and dependency folders (node_modules/, dist/…)
cook.no_examples: none yet; files written later follow the same rule
doctor.node.fix: install Node 22+ from https://nodejs.org and reopen your terminal.
doctor.hooks.missing: local hook entries are missing, invalid or point at a different install
doctor.hooks.fix: repair .claude/settings.local.json if invalid, then run verid upgrade --yes (verid cook for a new project).
doctor.hooks.ok: = Hooks point at this install's dist/
doctor.instructions.missing: {file}: the verid instruction block is missing or unreadable
doctor.instructions.edited: {file}: the verid instruction block was edited or has malformed markers
doctor.instructions.fix: Review the file, repair ambiguous markers if needed, then run {verid} upgrade --yes
doctor.plugins.repair: repair the record through Claude Code, or update verid if Claude Code uses a newer format.
doctor.plugins.permissions: check the file's permissions and Claude Code configuration folder.
doctor.plugins.reinstall: repair the record through Claude Code and reinstall the plugins.
doctor.plugin.missing: {name} does not look installed for this project
doctor.plugin.fix: run claude plugin marketplace add {source}, then claude plugin install {name}@{marketplace}.
doctor.agent.missing: {agent} is mapped to roles.{role}, but no installed {plugin} plugin for this project has that agent
doctor.agent.fix: update the plugin (verid's own: claude plugin marketplace update verid, then claude plugin update verid@verid), or map another agent in .verid/manifest.yaml.
doctor.manifest.cook: run verid cook in this project.
doctor.manifest.fix: inspect and repair .verid/manifest.yaml outside the agent.
doctor.repo.folder.fix: restore the folder or correct repos.path in .verid/manifest.yaml.
doctor.repo.git.missing: {repo} is not a Git repo or Git is not installed
doctor.repo.git.fix: install Git, then clone or initialize the repo in that folder.
doctor.repo.dirty: {repo} has uncommitted changes or Git could not read its status
doctor.repo.dirty.fix: run git status in that folder, then commit or stash your changes and resolve any Git errors.
doctor.repo.branch.mismatch: {repo} is on {branch}, which is neither main ({main}) nor a work branch, so commits there are refused
doctor.repo.branch.detached: {repo} has a detached HEAD, so commits and pushes there are refused
doctor.repo.branch.fix: switch to main, or to a work branch made from it whose name starts with feat/, fix/, chore/, docs/, refactor/ or test/, for example `git switch -c feat/<module>`.
doctor.repo.main: {repo}: main cannot be told ({detail}), so Git commands there are refused
doctor.repo.main.fix: set default_branch for the repo or git.default_branch in .verid/manifest.yaml, or make the first commit on main, from your own terminal.
doctor.module.history.fix: the module cannot close until this is fixed, as the message says.
doctor.repo.runner.fix: add a supported runner's build files, or set repos.test_cmd with {junit} in .verid/manifest.yaml.
doctor.architecture.idle: = Repo {repo}: architecture check {status}; no module waits to close, so this is not a problem yet
doctor.audit.broken: audit log {file}: the hash chain breaks at line {line}, so that entry or one before it was edited or removed
doctor.audit.fix: keep the file as evidence and find out who changed it; verid keeps appending, but the chain stays broken from that line.
doctor.architecture.fix: the agent runs `{verid} taste`, which runs the check after a passing suite; doctor never runs it.
VERID_BURNT_UPGRADE_NO_TERMINAL: verid upgrade needs --yes without a terminal. Use --dry-run to preview without writing.
cook.unlock_question: Which folders are locked? ◉ locked, ◯ unlocked.
cook.unlock_how: Type numbers to switch (e.g. 1,3), or a folder name to unlock; Enter keeps them as they are:
cook.invalid: That will not work: {detail}. Try again, or leave it empty to cancel.
command.tip: Ask to pass the action verid just blocked, once; verid gives you a code to confirm
command.confirm: Confirm an override with the code verid gave you
command.peek: Show where the TDD cycle stands and what it allows
command.menu: Show the plan, its modules and the next step
command.body: verid's hook handles this command and has answered above. If verid said nothing, its hooks are not registered on this machine: ask the developer to run `verid cook` from their terminal.
cook.served: Served! Open Claude Code and say what you want. The next step is always in: {verid} menu
cook.served_remix: Served! First run `{verid} stock` here: it records the tests that already fail as the baseline, and until then `{verid} taste` refuses to run. Then open Claude Code and say what you want. The next step is always in: {verid} menu
taste.setup: {runner} ({dir}) wrote no JUnit report: a tool or library may be missing. Install it with `{setup}`, then run `{verid} {command}` again.
taste.not_compiled: {runner} ({dir}) wrote no test report. When its output shows a compilation error, the tests did not compile: usually a new test calls a class or method that does not exist yet. verid reads the stub step only from a test report, never from the build's log, so ask the developer to allow the stub with `/verid tip <reason>`, write only the stub, then run `{verid} {command}` again.
taste.unsupported: Seen but not run by verid: {unsupported}; for those, the developer sets test_cmd in .verid/manifest.yaml.
serve.not_approved: it is not open: the developer approves it with `{verid} order` first
serve.already: it is not open: it was served already
serve.no_run: there is no valid run yet
serve.no_reviewer: no reviewer is mapped: add `roles.reviewer` to `.verid/manifest.yaml`, for example `verid:reviewer` (install it with `claude plugin marketplace add anhtranhai835/verid`, then `claude plugin install verid@verid`)
serve.no_review: no review of {module} since its last change: have the reviewer ({reviewer}) review it; verid records its final report when it stops; if Claude Code cannot find it, it is not installed (verid's own: `claude plugin marketplace add anhtranhai835/verid`, then `claude plugin install verid@verid`)
serve.review_stale: {module} changed after its review (a new commit, an amended message or an uncommitted change): have the reviewer ({reviewer}) review it again
git.commits: verid: repo {repo} has {count} commits since module {module} began. Several small, feature-scoped commits are valid. Keep each change coherent and verified; separate unrelated features. The squash merge leaves one commit on main.
commits.none: verid: no open module, so there is no module work to show.
commits.no_record: verid: where module {module}'s work began was not recorded, so its commits cannot be listed. In a human drive the developer runs `{verid} order {module}` again; an auto drive records it at the next stop.
git.no_history: verid: no Git history to check for module {module}: the project was not in Git when it was ordered.
serve.no_security: no passing security review of {module} since its last change: have the security reviewer ({security}) review it (verid:security); verid records its final report when it stops, and serves the module only when that report ends with `Verdict: pass`
serve.dirty: production code or a test changed that no run has seen
workspace.clone_failed: Repo {repo}: setup failed. Check its remote, default_branch and folder, then run verid cook again; existing folders are kept.
workspace.incomplete: Repo {repo}: existing folder is an incomplete clone from a failed or interrupted verid cook. Preserve any work, remove the folder and run verid cook again; the folder is kept.
workspace.done: verid is set up. Commit the shared files in .verid (git -C .verid status); root .claude/ files are generated on each machine. Keep {instructions} at the workspace root as per-machine files. cook regenerates their verid blocks. Open Claude Code at the workspace root.
mode.prep: Mode prep: agree the problem with verid:ba, design with verid:design, then modules with verid:plan. Build an approved module with verid:build.
mode.recipe: Mode recipe: read the existing specification with verid:ba; settle gaps through verid:design and verid:plan before verid:build.
mode.remix: Mode remix: preserve existing behaviour. The developer records old failures with `{verid} stock`; characterize untested code before changing it (verid:tdd).
session.log: Read it first to pick up where the last session stopped. After each AC, the main thread appends a dated entry: the AC, decisions and why, any deviation from the plan, commits, and what comes next. Subagents report to main.
session.menu: Full status, questions and audits: `{verid} menu`; cycle: `{verid} peek`.
session.single_writer_antigravity: Antigravity: main writes tests and code under the TDD gate; dispatch reviews with invoke_subagent to {reviewer} (security: {security}). Type /verid tip and /verid confirm in the chat for exceptions.
cook.antigravity_served: AGENTS.md is ready for Antigravity. Install the verid plugin once per machine with `{verid} setup-antigravity`, restart Antigravity, then run verid doctor.
init.antigravity_done: Antigravity instructions saved. Commit .verid/manifest.yaml, .verid/.gitignore and {instructions}. Each developer runs `{verid} setup-antigravity` once, and `{verid} cook` after cloning.
workspace.antigravity_done: Antigravity workspace instructions saved. Commit shared files inside .verid/ with `git -C .verid`; keep {instructions} at the workspace root as per-machine files. Each developer runs `{verid} setup-antigravity` once, and `{verid} cook` after cloning.
setup.antigravity_done: verid's Antigravity plugin is in {dir} ({created} created, {updated} updated, {kept} unchanged). Restart Antigravity, then run verid doctor in each project.
doctor.antigravity.plugin_missing: verid's Antigravity plugin is missing or stale on this machine
doctor.antigravity.plugin_fix: run verid setup-antigravity in your own terminal, then restart Antigravity
